reviews.comment: Tough grader with difficult exams and presentation, but quizzes were VERY easy and she offers so many opportunities for you to do well, coupled with an amazing curve at the end. C+ and C- on the exams, ended with an A- and didn't have to take the final. Decent lecturer but if you're not chem, chen, or msen, you might be a little lost (like I was).
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed CHEM 466. The course wasn't that bad, just make sure you do well on the first exam since subsequent exams tend to be more challenging. It's helpful to maintain a document of all polymer structures discussed for quick reference.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Learned a lot and enjoyed the class. She is very clear of her expectations and sets you up for success.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was always excited to talk about polymers, which made the class a lot more fun and interesting. Exams were a little rough, but the end-of-the-year project is a grade saver. There were 10 pop attendance quizzes, and she did an AMAZING curve at the end, she wants you to not have to take the final if you don't have to! Overall, 10/10!!
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wooley is incredibly successful and very smart, but this class was not very impressive. I learned a bit, but it wasn't organized great, and she seemed scattered during most lectures. It's a ton of just copying down structures with minimal interaction. You don't need to go to class because everything is recorded and posted. No homework.
If you have another choice, do NOT take this course. She is a great researcher but not a good instructor. Note is hard to read and the lecture goes very fast.

Dr. Wooley is a real gem in the chemistry department at TAMU! Highly accomplished chemist, incredible instructor, and extremely passionate about polymer chemistry. I've learned so much from her this semester and would absolutely recommend her to other chemistry students!

She's usually frazzled and goes through material quickly, but is a great prof. Goes through material in a way that students actually understand material rather than just relying on memorization. Exams are rough, but she's very fair in grading and curves exams. She's a really nice person in general and is helpful both in class and in office hours.
